concepts.template: fmt.Println("{text}")

const limit = 10
// TODO: rename limit and pick its value — a constant never changes while the program runs

value := 42
pointer := &value
// TODO: pointer holds value's address — *pointer reads and writes value itself
_ = pointer

jobs := make(chan int, 2)
jobs <- 1
close(jobs)
// TODO: closing tells receivers no more values are coming — they can still take what's already in

var count atomic.Uint64
count.Add(1)
// TODO: Add and Load are safe to call from many goroutines at once — no lock needed
_ = count.Load()

var mu sync.Mutex
mu.Lock()
// TODO: the shared thing only one goroutine at a time may touch goes here
mu.Unlock()
defer fmt.Println("TODO: a deferred call runs when the function around it returns — this one prints last")

text := "hello"
shouted := strings.ToUpper(text)
// TODO: the strings package holds Contains, Split, Join, Replace and friends
_ = shouted
log.Println("TODO: the message to log")

source: Gollemer's concept book — names of code mapped to their basic code. Rows are data, not grammar: add a row (id, names, kind, template) and the composer can assemble that concept in every phrasing its slots allow, with no new Go code. A malformed row is skipped; the rest of the book still loads.
